subject: Post-call: HeliumCare hosting priorities, network constraints & next NetOps steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marta Velez <marta@heliumcare.io>; HeliumCare IT <it@heliumcare.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & prioritized asks (hosting / VPC / air-gap)

Marta — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so the HeliumCare team has a single place to reference. Please flag anything we missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Regulatory: state-level PHI residency requirements across two US states; procurement requires evidence of deterministic data residency and audit trails.
- Network constraints: customer-managed bastion for inbound (no public IP on hosts), strict outbound proxy rules, and MTU limits across the private MPLS.
- Air-gap possibility: isolated on-prem option may be required for a small set of workloads (batch inference for PII-heavy datasets).

Goals (what success looks like)
1) Proof of concept running inference on a VPC-connected dedicated cluster (no egress outside region) within 6–8 weeks.
2) Clear security artifacts for procurement (SOC2 evidence, KMS integration notes, audit log examples).
3) Ops runbook for NetOps describing required firewall rules, proxy allowances, and VPN/peering handshake.

Open technical risks we called out
- Outbound proxy: our runtime needs to reach Redwood control plane endpoints for metrics and scheduling unless you want full private control-plane (private deployment).
- MTU and fragmentation: current packet size restrictions can degrade gRPC streaming; we flagged an alternative to use chunked HTTP streaming.

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA)
- HeliumCare: confirm whether the procurement team allows standard TLS egress to specific Redwood endpoints or if we must pursue private deployment (Marta — by 2026-07-02).
- Redwood (Ben): sketch minimal firewall/ACL list and suggested proxy exceptions — target 2026-07-01 for a NetOps-ready checklist.
- Redwood (Laura): share SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes + sample cloud config (today attached).
- Joint: schedule a 45-min NetOps deep-dive with HeliumCare network team + our infra SE (James from RackRegional included if helpful) — proposed dates 7/6 or 7/8.

Attachments:
- heliumcare_network_diagram_v1.pdf (you shared)
- redwood-hosting-options-one-pager.pdf (attached)
- SOC2-questions-answered.xlsx (attached)

If this aligns, I'll lock the NetOps slot and Ben will produce the firewall checklist. Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Marta Velez <marta@heliumcare.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: HeliumCare IT <it@heliumcare.io>; Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & prioritized asks (hosting / VPC / air-gap)

Thanks, Priyom — this is great and captures the discussion. A couple clarifications from procurement and our network team: 

1) Procurement: they will accept TLS egress if the endpoints are fixed CIDR blocks (not dynamic hostnames). Can you provide the minimal set of IP ranges and ports Redwood needs?

2) NetOps: we cannot open inbound ports to public hosts; any control-plane communication must be initiated from our side (outbound-only allowed) or go over a site-to-site VPN/peering.

3) Air-gap: for the small PII batch workload, we'd prefer a detachable on-prem appliance model (no connectivity to control plane). Is there a brief description of that workflow you can send?

We're ok to proceed with the NetOps deep-dive — please propose times and James Park (RackRegional) will join as our network architect.

— Marta
Marta Velez
Head of Compliance, HeliumCare
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marta Velez <marta@heliumcare.io>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & prioritized asks (hosting / VPC / air-gap)

Marta — quick note on the firewall/CIDR question. We're preparing a minimal egress CIDR set for the hosted control endpoints and a port list. High-level:
- TLS egress to 3 /24 blocks (control-plane API, metrics ingestion, package updates) on ports 443 and 5222 (if you prefer secure websockets).
- Health-checks: occasional UDP from monitoring agents; we can toggle to TCP-only if UDP is a blocker.
- For streaming inference, we recommend HTTP chunked streaming over port 443 to avoid MTU fragmentation.

I'll attach a short checklist for NetOps before the deep-dive. Also attaching a one-page note on our detachable on-prem workflow — it can operate in fully air-gapped mode (data never leaves customer network) but requires couriered package updates and a short initial bootstrap token exchange performed offline.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

- 10 min: Redwood control-plane connectivity options (hosted vs private)
- 15 min: NetOps checklist + firewall/CIDR confirmation (Ben)

Pre-work for the session:

If anything changes with attendees or timing, let me know. Looking forward to the deep-dive.
